Okay, now let's look at Hosea, who was active in the same period.
Hosea has quite a different feel from Amos.
Okay~ with Hosea, you have to look at chapter 1 carefully.
<호1:1> 웃시야와 요담과 아하스와 히스기야가 이어 유다 왕이 된 시대: <Hos 1:1> The word of the LORD that came unto Hosea, the son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.
히스기야 왕 때 북이스라엘은 나라가 망하는데 그리고 나서 이 글을 썼을:
Northern Israel fell in the time of King Hezekiah, and it's very likely this was written after that. At this time in Israel, people everywhere were serving other gods instead of God, doing things that made God angry.
 -
<호1:2> 여호와께서 비로소 호세아로 말씀하시니라 여호와께서 호세아에게: <Hos 1:2> The beginning of the word of the LORD by Hosea. And the LORD said to Hosea, Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms: for the land hath committed great whoredom, departing from the LORD.
- 특별한 시대에 특별한 명령. 언제 누구에게 하신 말씀인지 잘 분별할:
- A special command for a special time. You need to discern carefully when and to whom this was said. The whole nation had gone crazy serving Baal and Asherah.
 - How they saw the gods back then: usually a husband-and-wife pair of gods. They thought that if this couple got along well and had sex, the clouds would cover them, and then it would rain.
 - So they danced to make this divine couple want to have sex, and that was a strip show. This is the original.
 - The layout of the temple: built so people could have sex while the idol looked down on them. These rooms were called salons.
 - There were female priests dedicated entirely to doing this well: their name was Agnes. The Roman Catholic Church is copying it as is, right? Lots of nuns are named Agnes.
 - Gomer, the woman Hosea married, was someone who was very devoted to serving these gods.
<호1:3~5> 이에 저가 가서 디블라임의 딸 고멜을 취하였더니 저가 잉: <Hos 1:3~5> So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim; which conceived, and bare him a son. And the LORD said unto him, Call his name Jezreel; for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel. And it shall come to pass at that day, that I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel.
장자 이름을 이스르엘 이라고 지으라는 겁니다. 예후가 오므리 왕조를 심판: He tells him to name the firstborn son Jezreel. The place where Jehu judged the house of Omri was the plain of Jezreel, right? But now the house of Jehu is doing exactly what the house of Omri did, so God is saying He'll put an end to Jehu's dynasty too.
<호1:6> 고멜이 또 잉태하여 딸을 낳으매 여호와께서 호세아에게 이르시: <Hos 1:6> And she conceived again, and bare a daughter. And the LORD said unto Hosea, Call her name Lo-Ruhamah; for I will no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, that I should in any way pardon them.
장녀 : 로루하마 – 부정 접두어 ‘로’+ 긍휼 = 긍휼 없는 심판이: Firstborn daughter: Lo-Ruhamah – the negative prefix 'Lo' + mercy = there will be judgment without mercy.
<호1:8~9> 고멜이 로루하마를 젖뗀 후에 또 잉태하여 아들을 낳으매:
<Hos 1:8~9> Now when she had weaned Lo-Ruhamah, she conceived, and bare a son. Then said the LORD, Call his name Lo-Ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.
③ Second child: Lo-Ammi - Ammi means 'my people.' Not my people.
 - So in the end, the names of Hosea's three children mean: He will judge the house of Jehu, He will not show mercy, and the result is, I am completely not your God and you are not my people. Just like an angry father. "I'm taking you off the family register!"
And then right away come words of restoration. But they're mixed in with words of warning. 2:1, call them Ammi and Ruhamah. The main point is to get rid of the harlotry - the reason they served foreign gods was just in hopes of getting the things they needed... Serving foreign gods is useless. In the end everyone will come back. The day will come when she says, I will go back to my first husband.
8절 - 하나님의 기가 막힌 사연 또하나 : 백성들에게 은, 금, 재물을: Verse 8 - another of God's unbelievable stories: He gave the people silver, gold, and wealth, and they spent it on idol worship. It's like getting pocket money from your parents on Parents' Day and then going off to have fun with your girlfriend. Unbelievable, right...
3. 고멜을 통해 하나님의 마음을 이해하는 호세아: 3. Hosea understands God's heart through Gomer
3장에 보면 이 고멜이라는 여자가 처음부터 음란한 여자인데 하나님께서 데: In chapter 3, this woman Gomer was a promiscuous woman from the start, but God told him to take her and live with her. He thought maybe once they were married she'd settle down, but she couldn't drop that habit, and in no time she runs off after another man again...
그래서 그 남자를 수소문을 해서 찾아 갔더니 또 그 동안 보살핀 비용을: So he asks around, finds that man, and goes to him, and then the man demands to be paid for looking after her all that time. Paying a price to get back what's yours: that is exactly redemption. But once Hosea goes through this himself, he says he finally understands. So what he cries out at the top of his lungs is, 'Let us press on to know God.'
<호4:1~2> 이스라엘 자손들아 여호와의 말씀을 들으라 여호와께서 이: <Hos 4:1~2> Hear the word of the LORD, ye children of Israel: for the LORD hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land. By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood. (one after another)
<호4:6> 내 백성이 지식이 없으므로 망하는도다 네가 지식을 버렸으니:
<Hos 4:6> My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.
 - He will reject Israel, which has no knowledge of God. Then He rebukes the pagan practices the people of Israel were doing:
 - They ask their tree, and their staff answers... : fortune-telling
 - They sacrifice on the mountaintops and commit immorality under the shade of the trees.
 - Second half of verse 14: a people that doesn't understand will fall.
5장 - 우상 숭배에 대한 경고\n - 4절 : 음란한 마음이 있으면 여:
Chapter 5 - Warning about idol worship
 - Verse 4: if you have a spirit of harlotry, you can't know the LORD, and since you can't know the LORD, you can't return to God.
 - Verse 6: even if they bring cattle and sheep by the flock, they won't find God. Because He has already left... Solomon's prayer comes to nothing too. Then He warns that there will be war in Judah and Israel. If they lean on the great powers at that time, He will tear them apart like a lion does.
 - Verse 15: Israel, who only listens when you hit them
<호6:1~6> 오라 우리가 여호와께로 돌아가자 여호와께서 우리를 찢으셨:
<Hos 6:1~6> Come, and let us return unto the LORD: for he hath torn, and he will heal us; he hath smitten, and he will bind us up. After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight. Therefore let us know the LORD, let us press on to know the LORD: his going forth is sure as the morning; and he shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter rain that waters the earth. O Ephraim, what shall I do unto thee? O Judah, what shall I do unto thee? for your goodness is as a morning cloud, and as the early dew it goeth away. Therefore have I hewed them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of my mouth: and thy judgments are as the light that goeth forth. For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
 - What God wants, endlessly, is for us to know God. That's the theme of the book of Hosea.
치료하려고 했는데 오히려 죄악이 드러남. 맹장 수술하려고 배를 열었는데: He tried to heal them, but instead their sin came to light. It's like opening someone up for an appendix operation and finding a tumor. Israel's sin is pride, Ephraim's sin is mixing.
<호7:11> 에브라임은 어리석은 비둘기같이 지혜가 없어서 애굽을 향하여:
<Hos 7:11> Ephraim also is like a silly dove without heart: they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria.
 - The thing about doves is they find their way home, so a dove that can't find home has lost its mind. The prophet keeps urging them: don't look to Egypt, don't look to Assyria, look to God above.
<호7:13> 화 있을진저 저희가 나를 떠나 그릇 갔음이니라 패망할진저:
<Hos 7:13> Woe unto them! for they have fled from me: destruction unto them! because they have transgressed against me: though I would redeem them, yet they have spoken lies against me.
 - Redemption means paying an enormous price. God says He'll pay the whole price and redeem them, and still the people won't listen.
<호7:15> 내가 저희 팔을 연습시켜 강건케 하였으나 저희는 내게 대하:
<Hos 7:15> Though I have taught and strengthened their arms, yet they plot evil against me.
 - When He makes them a strong nation, they use that strength to do evil. With the arms God made, they whipped Jesus and nailed Him to the cross....
8장 - 우상숭배를 책망.\n - 이스라엘 : 금송아지 섬겼던 것:
Chapter 8 - Rebuke of idol worship
 - Israel: they served the golden calf
유다 : 제단은 많이 만들었음(죄 용서함은 받고 싶었던지),: Judah: they built lots of altars (I guess they wanted their sins forgiven),
그러나 자세하게 적어 준 율법은 이상히 여김: but the law He wrote out for them in detail, they treated as something strange
9장 - 벌 받는 날\n - 2절부터 보시면 포도주가 떨어질 것, 여호와:
Chapter 9 - The day of punishment
 - Look from verse 2: the wine will run out, they won't be able to live in the LORD's land,
에브라임은 애굽으로 갈 것이다. 종살이 하던 때 처럼 나락으로 떨어진다는: Ephraim will go to Egypt. That means falling back into the pit like when they were slaves. They will eat unclean things in Assyria.
<호9:10> 옛적에 내가 이스라엘 만나기를 광야에서 포도를 만남같이 하:
<Hos 9:10> I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness. I saw your fathers as the first ripe in the fig tree at its first season; but they came to Baal Peor, and consecrated themselves to the shameful thing, and became abominable like that which they loved.
 - It's a heartbreaking story. Israel would have quietly disappeared in Egypt, but God saved them, made a covenant at Mount Sinai like holding an engagement ceremony, and said, 'Now I have My own people too,' and God was really happy, you know? Israel was God's first love. But before He could even hold Israel in His arms once, they went and gave themselves disgracefully to Baal Peor and became as abominable as the idol. That's what He's saying (Numbers 25).
다른 배신도 가슴 아프지만 사랑을 배신하면 남이 되는게 아니라 원수가 된: Other betrayals hurt too, but when you betray love, you don't become strangers, you become enemies. So when God says He'll pour out His wrath, Hosea prays.
14절에 아이 배지 못하는 태와 젖 없는 유방을 달라고 하는 것은 그런: In verse 14, asking for a miscarrying womb and dry breasts means asking that, in such a horrible time, children would rather not be born at all.
16절 - 호세아의 기도를 듣지 않으심. 낳을지라도 죽여 버리겠다. 왜: Verse 16 - God doesn't listen to Hosea's prayer. Even if they give birth, I will kill them. Why go this far?
Verse 17 - Because they don't listen... in the end they become wanderers.
10장 - 경고\n - 늬들이 그렇게 좋아하는 제단들? 다 쳐서 없애 버:
Chapter 10 - Warning
 - Those altars you love so much? I'll smash them all and get rid of them. The words destruction and ruin come up a lot. Even so, look at verse 12: He says if they come back to God, He'll give them a chance. God really has no pride. You know, in a relationship, the one who loves more is the weaker one.
1~4절 이스라엘 역사 압축: Verses 1~4: Israel's history in a nutshell
<호11:1~2> 이스라엘의 어렸을 때에 내가 사랑하여 내 아들을 애굽에:
<Hos 11:1~2> When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt. The more they called them, the more they went from them; they sacrificed to the Baals, and burned incense to engraved images.
 - God called Israel out to point out what was wrong with the people of the world and to be missionaries to them, but they followed along and got converted themselves.
<호11:3~4> 그러나 내가 에브라임에게 걸음을 가르치고 내 팔로 안을:
<Hos 11:3~4> I taught Ephraim also to go, taking them by their arms; but they knew not that I healed them. I drew them with cords of a man, with bands of love: and I was to them as they that take off the yoke on their jaws, and I laid meat unto them.
 - God really did teach them to walk, and carried them in His arms, going along the wilderness road trying to fix them. He tried to fix the habits that had soaked into them in Egypt and make them holy, like God's people, like a kingdom of priests, but the training just didn't work. He tried pulling them with cords of love, He even let manna fall right in front of them, but no matter how hard He tried, it didn't work.
<호11:5> 저희가 애굽 땅으로 다시 가지 못하겠거늘 내게 돌아오기를:
<Hos 11:5> They shall not return into the land of Egypt; but because they refuse to return to me, the Assyrian shall be their king.
 - So if they still don't get it after all this, there's no choice but for the Assyrians, who repented after hearing Jonah's preaching, to be their king. He's saying, go to Assyria and learn a thing or two about how to repent. That's why He sends Shalmaneser in B.C. 722.
<호12:1> 에브라임은 바람을 먹으며 동풍을 따라가서 날마다 거짓과 포:
<Hos 12:1> Ephraim feedeth on wind, and followeth after the east wind: he daily increaseth lies and desolation; and they do make a covenant with the Assyrians, and oil is carried into Egypt.
 - Diplomacy, trade, saving the economy, those aren't what matter. What matters is knowing God and coming back to God. When you get too well off, serving God gets pretty hard. Even Jacob, whose conduct wasn't right, God met with him when he clung on weeping. So you come back too.
7절부터 보시면 또 기가 막힌 얘기 - 거짓 저울로 돈 벌면서 죄가 없다: Look from verse 7, another unbelievable story - they make money with false scales and say they have no sin. They have plenty of money, so maybe they offer calves as sacrifices, but that's useless. He's saying that unless they end their idol worship and pride, it won't work.
<호13:4~6> 그러나 네가 애굽 땅에서 나옴으로부터 나는 네 하나님:
<Hos 13:4~6> Yet I am the LORD thy God from the land of Egypt, and thou shalt know no god but me: for there is no saviour beside me. I did know thee in the wilderness, in the land of great drought. According to their pasture, so were they filled; they were filled, and their heart was exalted; therefore have they forgotten me.
 - The name Hosea means 'God is the Savior.' He filled them up, and they got proud and forgot God. You know, God has never once worried about us being poor. Rather, He worries that we'll get full and say we don't know Him. So the very fact that we're not rich is itself a blessing.
14장 - 호세아의 호소\n - 돌아오라!\n - 어떻게 돌아오느냐? 2:
Chapter 14 - Hosea's appeal
 - Come back!
 - How do you come back? Verse 2: Take with you words, and turn to the LORD: say unto him, Take away all iniquity, and receive what is good: instead of bulls we will offer the fruit of our lips to You. No more messing things up and then asking forgiveness with sacrifices; we'll offer the fruit of our lips.  We will not rely on Assyria to save us, we won't rely on the great powers.  We will not ride on horses, we'll stop the wars.  Neither will we say any more to the work of our hands, Ye are our gods. All this time we bowed to idols made with our own hands and served them as gods, but now we'll stop.  For in thee the fatherless findeth mercy. That's what to say.
He's saying, if you do that, I will restore you.
9절 누가 지혜가 있어 이런 일을 깨달으며 누가 총명이 있어 이런 일을: Verse 9: Who is wise, and he shall understand these things? prudent, and he shall know them? for the ways of the LORD are right, and the just shall walk in them: but the transgressors shall fall therein.  Judging by how Hosea wrote this, it seems no one among the people at the time understood. Because with the prophet Hosea as the last, Northern Israel falls.
